create.name: Dr. Rick Hanson
create.bio:
Rick Hanson is a psychologist and meditation teacher who brings together brain science and Buddhist practice. He has meditated since the mid-1970s, and his teaching draws openly on the insight tradition and on teachers such as Jack Kornfield, Tara Brach and Sylvia Boorstein. With the neurologist Rick Mendius he co-founded the Wellspring Institute, which looks at where neuroscience and contemplative practice meet, and he holds a senior fellowship at UC Berkeley's Greater Good Science Center. His books include Buddha's Brain, Hardwiring Happiness, Just One Thing, Resilient and Neurodharma.

At the centre of his approach is a simple idea: that by staying with good experiences a little longer, people gradually build lasting inner resources such as calm, contentment, kindness and a sense of worth. He calls this positive neuroplasticity and teaches it through a short four-step practice. His Neurodharma programme goes further, linking seven qualities found in deep contemplative states with what is known about the brain. Each Wednesday evening, Pacific time, he leads a free online meditation, talk and discussion that anyone may join, and he also offers recorded courses, a weekly newsletter of small practices and the Being Well podcast with his son Forrest.

books.title: Buddha's Brain: The Practical Neuroscience of Happiness, Love, and Wisdom
books.author: Rick Hanson
books.description: Written with the neurologist Rick Mendius, this book explains in plain terms what happens in the brain during contemplative practice, and offers exercises for steadying attention, warming the heart and growing insight.

books.title: Hardwiring Happiness: The New Brain Science of Contentment, Calm, and Confidence
books.author: Rick Hanson
books.description: Sets out his four-step way of turning passing good moments into lasting inner strengths, and explains why the mind tends to hold on to bad experiences more readily than good ones.

books.title: Just One Thing: Developing a Buddha Brain One Simple Practice at a Time
books.author: Rick Hanson
books.description: A collection of short practices, each one small enough to try in a day, for growing kindness, calm and steadiness in ordinary life.

books.title: Neurodharma: New Science, Ancient Wisdom, and Seven Practices of the Highest Happiness
books.author: Rick Hanson
books.description: Traces seven qualities found in deep meditation, from a steady mind to a sense of wholeness and timelessness, and pairs each with what is known about the brain and with practices to explore it.

books.title: Resilient: How to Grow an Unshakable Core of Calm, Strength, and Happiness
books.author: Rick Hanson, Forrest Hanson
books.description: Written with his son Forrest, it describes twelve inner strengths, such as compassion, grit and gratitude, and shows how to build each through everyday experience.

courses.title: Neurodharma Online Program
courses.description: An eight-week recorded programme with over fifteen hours of talks and six hours of guided practice. It explores seven qualities of deep contemplative life through Buddhist teaching and brain science.

courses.title: The Positive Neuroplasticity Training
courses.description: A six-week recorded course in his core method for turning good experiences into lasting inner strengths. It includes guided practices, a handbook and discussion forums; a version with professional education credits costs more.

courses.title: The Self-Worth Workshop
courses.description: A six-week recorded course on feeling at home in your own worth. Short talks, guided practices and a workbook focus on self-compassion, feeling cared about and letting go of harsh self-judgement.

courses.title: Just One Minute
courses.description: Fifty-seven very short practices, each introduced in a video of a minute or two, with an audio file, handout and weekly emails. The idea is to take up one small practice a day.

free_resources.title: Wednesday Meditations with Dr. Rick Hanson
free_resources.description: A free weekly session on Zoom each Wednesday evening, Pacific time: a guided meditation, a talk with questions, and optional small-group discussion. Recordings are available to those who sign up.

Health-rule borderline: his site's topic menu and several courses are framed by conditions (anxiety, depression, trauma, insecure attachment, grief, insomnia podcast episode); I judged his work mainly meditation and well-being teaching rather than condition-led, but the owner may disagree. All condition-named courses, talks and podcast episodes left out.
Political: his site has a 'Navigating Political Turmoil' topic page and he founded the Global Compassion Coalition; one topic among many, left out.
He is a psychologist (clinical practice now closed to new clients); listed for his meditation and Buddhist-informed teaching, not therapy.
Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock are named on his about page only in a list of organisations he is grateful to, not as places he teaches; no hub link added.
Contact is by form only; the page says personal questions cannot get individual replies.
